summary: Non-core imports in modules and plugins must be guarded so users get an actionable error instead of a traceback, and so Ansible can import code for docs and inspection without all requirements installed.
questions: Why must modules guard third-party imports?

answer_card.title: Why guard imports
answer_card.answer_md: Ansible runs across many hosts and interpreters. Guarding non-core imports avoids confusing tracebacks, and `missing_required_lib` tells the user which library is missing, on which host, for which interpreter. It also lets Ansible import code for docs and testing without installing every dependency.
